## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')

Let me plan the game. A 2D Street Fighter duel — single HTML file (canvas game) with:

- Two fighters, player vs AI
- Health bars, timer, rounds, "K.O." 
- Three special moves with inputs (quarter-circle forward punch, etc.) — plus projectile, uppercut, spinning kick? Three specials:
  1. Hadouken (fireball) — QCF + punch, projectile
  2. Shoryuken (dragon punch) — F,D,DF + punch, invincible rising uppercut
  3. Tatsumaki (spinning kick) — QCB + kick, multi-hit spinning kick moving forward
  
Also normals: light punch, heavy punch, light kick, heavy kick. Blocking (hold back). Crouch, jump. AI opponent. Super meter? Keep reasonable scope but polished.

Visual style: canvas 2D with gradient sky, sunset city, parallax, silhouettes, particles. Fighters drawn procedurally with limbs — a stick-figure-ish muscular style with rounded capsules. That's the hard part to look good. Use vector limbs with joints for punch/kick animations, plus character-specific colors and head designs.

I'll implement a fighter renderer using capsule segments with IK-ish pose keyframes per state. Actually simpler: define pose per animation frame as angles for torso, arms, legs, and draw segments. Use procedural animation with sin-based idle bob, and pose interpolation for attacks.

Controls:
- Desktop: A/D move, W jump, S crouch, J light punch, K heavy punch, L kick, hold back to block. Arrows also. Specials via motion inputs (QCF etc.) or simplify: keyboard sequence detection. Also add dedicated special keys? For accessibility maybe list move inputs. Motion input on keyboard is doable: track directional history with timestamps and check patterns.
- Mobile: virtual joystick + 4 buttons (LP, HP, K, Special/Super). Motion inputs on touch are hard; add special buttons: fireball/uppercut/spin as three tap buttons. Better: three special buttons on mobile directly. On desktop, both motion inputs and hotkeys (U/I/O?) maybe. Let's use: specials on desktop via motion inputs, and also show them in move list. Actually simplest reliable: give three special buttons visible on mobile, and on desktop keys "1/2/3" plus motion inputs for authenticity.

Combat mechanics: health 1000, hitstun, blockstun, chip damage, knockback, juggle, combo counter, super meter fills on damage dealt/taken, round timer 60s, best of 3, KO screen, rematch. Hitboxes: rectangle-based per attack keyframe with damage, hitstun, blockable high/low, knockback, active frames. Projectile fireball entity.

Let's design code architecture in a single game.js (maybe split into files: index.html, styles.css, game.js modules). Simpler: index.html + css + js modules (engine.js, fighter.js, ai.js, render.js). Keep it manageable: index.html, style.css, js/ files. Since static server handles ES modules fine.

Plan files:
- index.html — canvas, HUD overlay (DOM for health bars/timer/menu), touch controls.
- css/style.css
- js/main.js — boot, loop, input
- js/fighter.js — Fighter class, moves, physics
- js/ai.js — AI opponent
- js/render.js — background + fighter drawing, particles
- js/audio.js — WebAudio SFX (punch, hit, fireball, KO, hadouken voice? synthesized). Keep simple synthesized sounds.

HUD: health bars with delayed damage trail, timer, round pips, super meter, combo popups, "FIGHT!", "K.O.", "ROUND 1", character names.

Fighter visuals: Let's do a stylized "neon dojo" look: characters with defined shirtless torso, gi pants, belt, headband, gloves. Drawn with limbs from shoulder/elbow/hand positions computed by forward kinematics from angles. That can look decent if proportions are right.

Approach: define skeleton with joints in local coordinates:
- pelvis at (0,0) ground-relative.
- torso lean, head.
- shoulders L/R, elbows, hands, hips, knees, feet.

For a side view (facing +x), draw far limbs slightly darker behind torso, near limbs in front. Use capsule drawing (line with round caps) of thick width.

Poses: define keyframes as joint angle sets. Easier: define target positions for hands/feet directly per pose (in local space), then solve two-bone IK for elbow/knee. That's nice: for each animation pose, specify hip Y offset, torso angle, hand positions, feet positions. Two-bone IK with bend direction. Good for punches (hand extends forward), kicks (foot forward), crouch (hip lower), jump (feet tucked).

Let me implement:
- local coordinate: x forward (facing right for P1 after transform; if facing left, mirror x).
- Origin at pelvis, y up positive? Canvas y down. I'll use world with y up in drawing helper, converting. Simpler: define in canvas coords with y down but pelvis at hip height; feet at +y.

Let's use "unit" space where 1 unit = 1 px roughly at scale 1. Fighter height ~170 px. pelvis at y=-70 relative to feet ground. Head at -160. Shoulders at -130. Arms length upper 26, fore 26. Legs thigh 38, shin 38.

IK: given shoulder S, target hand H, lengths a,b, bend sign -> compute elbow via law of cosines.

Pose definitions (local, relative to pelvis at (0,0), y down positive):
- hipOffset y: pelvis relative to ground (standard 70).
- torso lean angle.
- hands: {x,y} relative to pelvis; shoulders computed from torso.
- feet: {x,y} relative to pelvis ground (i.e., absolute offsets), use for IK from hips.

Actually both arms and legs via IK targets relative to pelvis is convenient.

Pose fields:
```
{ hip: 70, lean: 0.06, headTilt: 0,
  Lhand:{x:-18,y:10}, Rhand:{x:-4,y:18},  // guard near chest
  Lfoot:{x:-22,y:70}, Rfoot:{x:16,y:70},
  bendArms:[1,1], bendLegs:[1,1] }
```
Facing right means forward = +x. Guard hands in front (x positive). Let me define forward positive and draw with scale flip.

Idle pose: hands up near face: near hand (front) at x=26,y=-18 (chest/face), far hand x=14,y=-6. Feet apart: front foot x=20,y=0, back foot x=-24,y=0. Pelvis at ground -70 => feet targets relative pelvis y=+70.

Animations keyframes per state with time normalized: e.g., punch: windup (hand pulled back), active (hand extended to x=70,y=-25), recovery. Interpolate.

Attacks:
Normals:
- LP: jab, fast 5f startup, 3f active, 6f recovery, dmg 40, range short, frame advantage.
- HP: heavy straight, 10f startup, dmg 90, knockback.
- LK: low kick (crouching kick?) Let's have Kick (MK): mid kick 8f, dmg 70.
- Crouch attacks: crouch + punch = low, crouch+kick = sweep (knockdown).
- Air attacks: jump + punch/kick.

Specials:
1. Hadouken (Fireball): 236 + P. Projectile with speed 520 px/s, dmg 110, blockable, chip 15.
2. Shoryuken: 623 + P. Rising uppercut, invincible 8f, dmg 150, launches.
3. Tatsumaki Senpukyaku (Hurricane Kick): 214 + K. Multi-hit spinning kick moving forward, 3 hits x 45.

Super: 236236+P when meter full? Add super as bonus ("Metsu Hadouken") — could be 4th. Request says three special moves, so keep three specials + optional super? Might overcomplicate. I'll implement exactly three specials, and the super meter boosts special damage/visuals when full? Simpler: meter gives "Overdrive": when full, press the three special keys together? Skip. Let's make super meter power up specials (EX versions) — press S? Hmm.

Keep: three specials, EX versions when meter full using double-tap of that special key. Might be confusing. I'll do: meter fills; when full, specials become EX (extra damage + bigger visuals) automatically and meter drains, with a "SUPER READY" glow. That's simple and fun.

AI: state machine with approach/retreat/attack/block/jump, difficulty ramps per round. Reacts to projectiles (jump or block), punishes whiffs sometimes, has cooldowns.

Physics: positions x (world), y (height above ground 0), vx, vy, facing. Ground at y=0 (feet). Stage bounds x in [60, 900] with stage width maybe 1300 and camera? Camera scrolling adds complexity. Use fixed stage 1152x648 canvas with fighters constrained x in [90, 1062]. Canvas scaled to fit viewport (16:9), HUD DOM overlay scaled? Simpler: draw everything on canvas including HUD, and canvas scaled with CSS to fit. That guarantees consistent layout and mobile responsiveness. Round rect health bars drawn in canvas. Touch controls as DOM overlay buttons at bottom outside? Overlay on canvas bottom corners. On mobile, drawing joystick/buttons as DOM divs positioned above canvas is fine.

Better to render canvas at fixed 1280x720 internal resolution and letterbox with CSS (object-fit). Touch controls overlay absolutely positioned over the canvas, sized responsively. The canvas area 16:9; on 390x844 portrait, the game will be small with big empty top/bottom. Instead, use portrait layout: rotate? Common approach: full-screen canvas with aspect ratio adaptive, game world rendered with camera scale to fit. Let's make canvas fill screen, render world with a scale so the whole 1280x720 wide scene fits... In portrait, fitting width 1280 -> height 720*(390/1280)=219px game area; plenty of vertical space for controls beneath. That's acceptable: HUD top, arena center, big touch controls bottom. Draw letterboxed canvas full width, vertically centered slightly above the controls. I'll make canvas fill container that is full screen with the arena letterboxed, and overlay touch controls in the lower area.

Simpler and robust: canvas fills window (portrait or landscape), internal render resolution = window size * dpr, and render the scene with a fit transform that shows world 1280x720 letterboxed. HUD as canvas-drawn in world coords. Touch overlay positioned over bottom parts of the screen; in portrait they overlap letterbox black bars mostly.

Game states: title/menu (with character select? maybe just two chars: Ryu-like "Kaze" and "Ken-like"? Let's give player a character choice? Keep single matchup: KAZE vs REN, two distinct palettes). Menu screen with "PRESS ENTER / TAP TO FIGHT", controls list, difficulty toggle? Add 3 difficulty options maybe. Keep it: Start screen with quick controls; pause with Esc; game over screen with rematch.

Let me also add round system: first to 2 rounds. Timer 60s. Round intro: "ROUND 1 / FIGHT!". KO: slow-mo + freeze, "K.O." then next round.

Effects: hit sparks (particles), screen shake, hitstop (freeze frames), dust on landing/dash, speed lines during specials, chromatic flash on KO.

Audio: WebAudio synth: whoosh, punch impact, block, fireball, DP, KO, round announce (speech synthesis? no—use tones), menu click. Plus a simple looping beat? Maybe a light synthwave loop with bass arpeggio using oscillators, toggleable mute. Nice polish but can be annoying; I'll add music toggle default on low volume? Keep SFX only + ambient crowd? SFX only, with mute button M.

Let's now write the code. Roughly:
- 3500+ lines total maybe. Let's be organized and careful.

Let me define detailed engine.

Coordinates: world units, ground y=0 means feet baseline at y=0. Canvas maps world: the stage floor line at y=600 in a 1280x720 view. I'll define a camera transform: worldToScreen(x, y) where x is stage coordinate 0..1280, y is height above ground (0 at feet, positive up). So screenX = x, screenY = FLOOR_Y - y. Fighters drawn with feet at FLOOR_Y - y.

Fighter state:
```
{
 x, y (height), vx, vy, facing (1/-1),
 hp, maxHp 1000,
 state: 'idle'|'walk'|'crouch'|'jump'|'attack'|'block'|'hitstun'|'blockstun'|'knockdown'|'ko'|'intro'|'win',
 stateTime,
 move: currentMove object,
 hitstun, blockstun,
 attackHasHit: Set (for multihit use hitIds),
 meter 0..100,
 airborne, 
}
```
Frame-based simulation at 60fps fixed step with accumulator. Attacks defined in frames.

Move definition:
```
{
 name, startup, active, recovery, damage, chip, hitstun, blockstun, knockdown,
 hitbox: (per frame?) {offsetX, y, w, h},
 knockback: {x,y}, launch: bool, meterGain, 
 motion / type, sound, 
 anim: keyframes function(progress) -> pose
}
```
Use phase progress: t in [0, startup+active+recovery). Active window. Hitbox activated during active.

Hitbox in local coords relative to fighter pelvis: rect {x (forward offset from center), y (height above ground), w, h}. Check overlap with opponent hurtbox (body rect ~ width 50, height 150, adjusted crouch 95) and block check: opponent holding back and not in attack/hitstun and grounded (or air-block disabled). If blocking -> blockstun, chip damage for specials only, pushback. If crouching and attack is 'overhead' -> hit. Low attacks must be blocked crouching. Crouch block: opponent crouching while holding back blocks low; standing block blocks overhead but not low.

Jumps: gravity 2100 px/s², initial vy 780, air control small. Jump duration ~0.75s.

Walk speed 210 px/s forward, 170 backward. Crouch reduces hurtbox.

Pushback: fighters can't overlap: min distance 58; push each other apart when both grounded and idle/walk.

Facing: auto-face opponent when grounded and not attacking.

Meter: gain on dealing/taking damage & whiffing specials. Max 100. When full, specials auto-EX and consume.

Round timer 60s, decrement; time out -> higher HP wins round.

Now motion input detection: buffer of directional presses with timestamps:
- Directions from keys: held back/forward/down. For QCF: need down, downforward, forward sequence within 400ms. Since keyboard has only down + forward, sequence: down (maybe with forward = downforward), forward. Detection: track history of states {dir: 'd','df','f','n'} changes. For 236: d, df, f. Keyboard can hold down then press forward => df, then release down => f. So players do ↓ then ↓↘ then →. Using both keys we get that. Check history ends with f and within 500ms contained d before f. Good.

Dragon punch 623: f, d, df within 500ms. Hurricane 214: d, db, b. Back = away from opponent.

But on keyboard, quarter circle inputs are finicky; also add simple shortcuts: double-tap? I'll add intuitive special keys on desktop too: U = Fireball, I = Uppercut, O = Spin Kick. And display "or U / I / O". P1 keys: A/D move, W jump, S crouch, J light punch, K heavy punch, L kick. Specials U/I/O. That's a lot of keys but fine. Mobile: joystick + LP, HP, K, and 3 special buttons (small). Actually mobile: d-pad and buttons LP, HP, K, and special buttons row.

IK math:
```
function ik(a, b, root, target, bend) {
  let dx = target.x-root.x, dy = target.y-root.y;
  let d = clamp(len, ...); 
  let d0 = Math.min(Math.max(dist, abs(a-b)+1), a+b-1);
  let ang = atan2(dy,dx);
  let cosA = (a*a + d0*d0 - b*b)/(2*a*d0);
  let A = Math.acos(clamp(cosA,-1,1));
  let jointAng = ang - bend*A; // bend=+1 => rotate one way
  return {x: root.x + cos(jointAng)*a, y: root.y + sin(jointAng)*a};
}
```

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D Street Fighter-style duel game featuring three special moves.

## Requirements
- Create a complete playable game, not a static mockup.
- Include three special moves.
- Keep it playable in desktop and mobile layouts.

## Decisions
- Used a synthwave street-fighter presentation with KAZE versus REN.
- Added keyboard and touch controls.
- Implemented synthesized audio with no external assets.
- Used a 1280×720 responsive canvas and mobile controls.
- Added EX special versions activated when the meter reaches 100%.

### Completed
- Built the title screen, fighter selection presentation, HUD, pause/results screens, and responsive touch controls.
- Implemented match logic, health, meter, rounds, AI difficulty, KO, win, and rematch flows.
- Implemented basic movement, jumping, blocking, crouching, punches, and kicks.
- Implemented fireball, rising special, and spinning special moves.
- Added animated arena, fighters, effects, hit sparks, projectiles, particles, and synthesized sound.
- Added desktop keyboard and mobile touch input.
- Added local fonts and visual assets.
- Ran browser checks and saved screenshots in `/tmp/neon-shots`.

### Active
- None.

- None.

1. Start the server and verify the latest build in a browser.
2. Run a final desktop and mobile interaction pass.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main page structure and UI screens.

290: export function poseForMove(move, time) {
291:   const anim = move.anim;
292:   if (!anim || anim.length === 0) return BASE[move.poseKind] || STAND;
293:   if (time <= anim[0].t) return anim[0];
294:   if (time >= anim[anim.length - 1].t) return anim[anim.length - 1];
295:   for (let i = 0; i < anim.length - 1; i++) {
296:     const a = anim[i];
297:     const b = anim[i + 1];
298:     if (time >= a.t && time <= b.t) {
299:       const span = b.t - a.t || 1;
300:       const u = (time - a.t) / span;
301:       const e = u * u * (3 - 2 * u);
302:       return {
303:         hipY: a.hipY + (b.hipY - a.hipY) * e,
304:         lean: a.lean + (b.lean - a.lean) * e,
305:         tilt: a.tilt + (b.tilt - a.tilt) * e,
306:         rot: a.rot + (b.rot - a.rot) * e,
307:         offY: (a.offY || 0) + ((b.offY || 0) - (a.offY || 0)) * e,
308:         handF: {
309:           x: a.handF.x + (b.handF.x - a.handF.x) * e,
310:           y: a.handF.y + (b.handF.y - a.handF.y) * e,

312:         handB: {
313:           x: a.handB.x + (b.handB.x - a.handB.x) * e,
314:           y: a.handB.y + (b.handB.y - a.handB.y) * e,

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable 2D Street Fighter-style duel game with three special moves.

## Requirements
- Provide a complete playable game rather than a static mockup.
- Include fireball, rising, and spinning special moves, plus EX versions at 100% meter.
- Support desktop and mobile layouts with keyboard and touch controls.
- Keep the game fully synthesized with no external assets.
- Use a 1280×720 responsive canvas presentation.

## Decisions
- Use the synthwave street-fighter setting “NEON FIST,” featuring KAZE versus REN.
- Provide normal attacks, movement, jumping, blocking, crouching, rounds, AI difficulty, KO, pause, mute, rematch, and results flows.
- Preserve the existing local fonts and visual assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built title, fighter-selection, HUD, pause, and results presentation.
- Implemented match logic, health, meter, rounds, AI, KO, win, and rematch flows.
- Implemented movement, jumping, blocking, crouching, jab, heavy punch, and kick.
- Implemented all three specials and EX special activation.
- Implemented arena, fighters, projectiles, hit sparks, particles, animation, and synthesized sound.
- Added keyboard and touch controls.
- Verified desktop and mobile title/fight layouts, movement, blocking, jumps, attacks, specials, EX meter, pause, mute, and rematch in Chromium.
- Verified the round-transition and match-end logic directly by applying KO damage.
- Served and tested the game at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Saved browser screenshots in `/tmp/neon-shots`.

### Active
- Final interaction pass only: complete full browser automation for all previously forced/edge-case flows if needed.
- Validate the remaining automated KO/round and results sequences as runtime evidence, since direct KO testing succeeded.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Re-run the consolidated end-to-end browser check and address only reproducible failures.
2. Confirm fireball projectile spawning, jab/spin activation, all three specials, pause, mute, KO, round transitions, and rematch in one run.
3. Perform a final desktop and mobile visual pass.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main page structure and screens.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: Match, combat, rounds, and AI orchestration.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/fighter.js`: Fighter movement, damage, state, and meter logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/moves.js`: Move definitions and hitbox data.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: Keyboard and touch input.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/render.js`: HUD, arena, fighter, and effect rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: Boot, frame loop, screens, and input wiring.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: Responsive desktop/mobile styling.

## Important Context
- `window.__neonFist` exposes `{ game, renderer, sfx, input }` for debugging and automation.
- Desktop controls are arrows or WASD for movement, J jab, K heavy punch, L kick, and U/I/O for specials.
- P or Escape pauses, M toggles mute, and Enter/Space starts.
- Browser verification found no desktop or mobile console/page errors.
- A KO can be produced directly with `g.applyStrike(g.player, g.cpu, {...damage...}, g.cpu.x, 500);`.
- Direct KO verification confirmed `state === "roundEnd"`, CPU `state === "ko"`, `player.wins === 1`, followed by round 2 at 1000 HP.

290: export function poseForMove(move, time) {
291:   const anim = move.anim;
292:   if (!anim || anim.length === 0) return BASE[move.poseKind] || STAND;
293:   if (time <= anim[0].t) return anim[0];
294:   if (time >= anim[anim.length - 1].t) return anim[anim.length - 1];
295:   for (let i = 0; i < anim.length - 1; i++) {
296:     const a = anim[i];
297:     const b = anim[i + 1];
298:     if (time >= a.t && time <= b.t) {
299:       const span = b.t - a.t || 1;
300:       const u = (time - a.t) / span;
301:       const e = u * u * (3 - 2 * u);
302:       return {
303:         hipY: a.hipY + (b.hipY - a.hipY) * e,
304:         lean: a.lean + (b.lean - a.lean) * e,
305:         tilt: a.tilt + (b.tilt - a.tilt) * e,
306:         rot: a.rot + (b.rot - a.rot) * e,
307:         offY: (a.offY || 0) + ((b.offY || 0) - (a.offY || 0)) * e,
308:         handF: {
309:           x: a.handF.x + (b.handF.x - a.handF.x) * e,
310:           y: a.handF.y + (b.handF.y - a.handF.y) * e,
311:         },
312:         handB: {
313:           x: a.handB.x + (b.handB.x - a.handB.x) * e,
314:           y: a.handB.y + (b.handB.y - a.handB.y) * e,
315:         },
316:         footF: {
317:           x: a.footF.x + (b.footF.x - a.footF.x) * e,
318:           y: a.footF.y + (b.footF.y - a.footF.y) * e,
319:         },
320:         footB: {
321:           x: a.footB.x + (b.footB.x - a.footB.x) * e,
322:           y: a.footB.y + (b.footB.y - a.footB.y) * e,
323:         },
324:       };
325:     }
326:   }
327:   return anim[anim.length - 1];
328: }

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable 2D Street Fighter-style duel game with three special moves.

## Requirements
- Provide a complete playable game rather than a static mockup.
- Include fireball, rising, and spinning special moves, plus EX versions at 100% meter.
- Support desktop and mobile layouts with keyboard and touch controls.
- Keep the game fully synthesized with no external assets.
- Use a 1280×720 responsive canvas presentation.
- Include normal attacks, movement, jumping, blocking, crouching, rounds, AI difficulty, KO, pause, mute, rematch, and results flows.

## Decisions
- Use the synthwave street-fighter setting “NEON FIST,” featuring KAZE versus REN.
- Preserve the existing local fonts and visual assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built title, fighter-selection, HUD, pause, and results presentation.
- Implemented match logic, health, meter, rounds, AI, KO, win, and rematch flows.
- Implemented movement, jumping, blocking, crouching, jab, heavy punch, and kick.
- Implemented all three specials and EX special activation.
- Implemented arena, fighters, projectiles, hit sparks, particles, animation, and synthesized sound.
- Added keyboard and touch controls.
- Verified desktop and mobile title/fight layouts, movement, blocking, jumps, attacks, specials, EX meter, pause, mute, and rematch in Chromium.
- Verified round-transition and match-end logic directly by applying KO damage.
- Served and tested the game at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Saved browser screenshots in `/tmp/neon-shots`.
- Direct KO verification confirmed `state === "roundEnd"`, CPU `state === "ko"`, `player.wins === 1`, followed by round 2 at 1000 HP.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the consolidated end-to-end browser check for all special moves, pause, mute, KO, round transitions, and rematch.
2. Perform a final desktop and mobile visual pass.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main page structure and screens.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: Match, combat, rounds, and AI orchestration.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/fighter.js`: Fighter movement, damage, state, and meter logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/moves.js`: Move definitions and hitbox data.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: Keyboard and touch input.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: Boot, frame loop, screens, and input wiring.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: Responsive desktop/mobile styling.

## Important Context
- `window.__neonFist` exposes `{ game, renderer, sfx, input }` for debugging and automation.
- Desktop controls are arrows or WASD for movement, J jab, K heavy punch, L kick, and U/I/O for specials.
- P or Escape pauses, M toggles mute, and Enter/Space starts.
- A KO can be produced directly with `g.applyStrike(g.player, g.cpu, {...damage...}, g.cpu.x, 500);`.
